title: Anti-Neuroinflammatory Effects of Prenylated Indole Alkaloids from the Antarctic Fungus Aspergillus sp. Strain SF-7367.
authors: Liu, Zhiming; Yoon, Chi-Su; Cao, Thao Quyen; Lee, Hwan; Kim, Il-Chan; Yim, Joung Han; Sohn, Jae Hak; Lee, Dong-Sung; Oh, Hyuncheol
one_liner_zh: 该文研究南极真菌代谢物对神经炎症的抑制作用，涉及NF-κB信号通路和分子对接，但核心是天然产物抗炎药理，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Inflammation has always been considered a trigger or consequence of neurodegenerative diseases, and the inhibition of inflammation in the central nervous system can effectively protect nerve cells. Several studies have indicated that various natural products inhibit neuroinflammation. Among these, Antarctic fungal metabolites have pharmacological activities and a developmental value. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the anti-neuroinflammatory activity of an Antarctic fungus belonging to Aspergillus (strain SF-7367). Secondary metabolites of SF-7367 were isolated using high-performance liquid chromatography followed by validation of their anti-inflammatory effects in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated BV2 microglia and RAW264.7 macrophages. Chemical analysis of metabolites from the fungal strain revealed five known compounds: epideoxybrevianamide E (1), brevianamide V/W (2), brevianamide K (3), brevianamide Q (4), and brevianamide R (5). Among these compounds, brevianamide K showed significant anti-inflammatory activity against both cell types. Results of Western blotting and molecular docking showed that brevianamide K could regulate the activation of nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cell (NF-kappaB) signaling. This indicates that brevianamide K present in Aspergillus sp. (strain SF-7367) can inhibit inflammatory responses by reducing lipopolysaccharide-induced nuclear translocation of NF-kappaB (p65). These findings suggest that Aspergillus sp. (strain SF-7367) and brevianamide K are candidate agents for treating neurodegenerative diseases.
abstract_zh: 炎症一直被认为是神经退行性疾病的触发因素或后果，而抑制中枢神经系统的炎症可有效保护神经细胞。多项研究表明，多种天然产物能抑制神经炎症，其中南极真菌代谢物具有药理活性和开发价值。因此，本研究旨在评估一种属于曲霉属（Aspergillus，菌株SF-7367）的南极真菌的抗神经炎症活性。采用高效液相色谱法分离SF-7367的次级代谢产物，并在脂多糖刺激的BV2小胶质细胞和RAW264.7巨噬细胞中验证其抗炎效果。对该真菌菌株代谢物的化学分析揭示了五种已知化合物：epideoxybrevianamide E (1)、brevianamide V/W (2)、brevianamide K (3)、brevianamide Q (4) 和 brevianamide R (5)。在这些化合物中，brevianamide K 对两种细胞类型均表现出显著的抗炎活性。Western blotting 和分子对接结果表明，brevianamide K 可调节核因子κB（NF-kappaB）信号通路的激活。这表明，曲霉属（菌株SF-7367）中的brevianamide K 可通过减少脂多糖诱导的NF-kappaB（p65）核转位来抑制炎症反应。这些发现提示，曲霉属（菌株SF-7367）和brevianamide K 是治疗神经退行性疾病的候选药物。
